nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a field, $I$ an ideal of $k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$, and $P, v \in k^n$. Then $v$ lies in the tangent space of $I$ at $P$ if and only if, for every $f \in I$, the total derivative of $f$ at $P$ along $v$ is zero.
nodes.title: Membership in the tangent space of an ideal

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a field, $f \in k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$, and $P, v \in k^n$. Then $v$ lies in the tangent space of the hypersurface $f = 0$ at $P$ if and only if the total derivative of $f$ at $P$ along $v$ is zero.
nodes.title: Membership in the tangent space of a hypersurface

nodes.summary: For a field $k$, an ideal $I$ of $k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ and a point $P \in k^n$, the tangent space of $I$ at $P$ is the $k$-linear subspace of $k^n$ obtained as the intersection, over all $f \in I$, of the tangent spaces at $P$ of the hypersurfaces $f = 0$. The point $P$ is not required to be a common zero of $I$.
nodes.title: Tangent space of an ideal

nodes.summary: For a field $k$, a polynomial $f \in k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ and a point $P \in k^n$, the tangent space of the hypersurface $f = 0$ at $P$ is the kernel of the total derivative of $f$ at $P$, viewed as a $k$-linear map $k^n \to k$: the subspace of vectors $v \in k^n$ with $\sum_{i=1}^n \frac{\partial f}{\partial x_i}(P)\, v_i = 0$. The point $P$ is not required to satisfy $f(P) = 0$.
nodes.title: Tangent space of a hypersurface

nodes.summary: For a field $k$, a polynomial $f \in k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ and $P, v \in k^n$, the total derivative of $f$ at $P$, viewed as a $k$-linear map $k^n \to k$, sends $v$ to the total derivative of $f$ at $P$ along $v$.
nodes.title: Evaluating the total derivative linear map

nodes.summary: For a field $k$, a polynomial $f \in k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ and a point $P \in k^n$, this is the $k$-linear map $k^n \to k$ sending $v$ to the total derivative of $f$ at $P$ along $v$, namely $\sum_{i=1}^n \frac{\partial f}{\partial x_i}(P)\, v_i$.
nodes.title: Total derivative as a linear map

nodes.summary: For a field $k$, a polynomial $f \in k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ and $P, v \in k^n$, the total derivative of $f$ at $P$ along the translated direction $v$ is $\sum_{i=1}^n \frac{\partial f}{\partial x_i}(P)\, v_i \in k$, where $\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_i}$ is the formal partial derivative.
nodes.title: Total derivative at a point

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
